To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a novel 3'–BCL11B (rs8022678) gene desert locus, which modulates the effect of sodium on blood pressure, and that rs8022677 A carriers may receive greater benefit from sodium-reduction interventions.

we have identified a novel gene desert locus, the 3′ end of BCL11B, which modulates the effect of daily sodium consumption on systolic blood pressure, and that this locus may be used to classify persons into sodium-sensitivity subgroups.

a genome-wide interaction study identified a novel 3' BCL11B gene deserts locus as a novel locus that interacts with sodium intake to affect blood pressure, which is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a personalized medicine strategy for sodium reduction.
the identification of a novel gene desert locus that may contribute to the development of sodium-sensitive hypertension.
the identification of genetic loci that modulate sodium effect on blood pressure and the development of a novel strategy for personalized prevention of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3′BCL11B region may be a genetic determinant of sodium sensitivity.
the 3′ BCL11B gene locus may be involved in the sodium-blood pressure relationship.
a novel 3’-BCL11A gene desert locus was associated with blood pressure, and the association was dependent on sodium intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rs8022768 A carriers may be a high-risk group for sodium-induced hypertension and that the rs802278 A non-carriers are not.
a genetic variant in a 3′-gene desert of BCL11B gene, which is located at chromosome 2q13.1, was associated with the interaction effect of daily sodium consumption and systolic blood pressure.
a genetic test for rs8022678 may provide a complementary role to population approaches in sodium reduction strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genome-wide interaction analysis can detect genetic variants associated with complex traits that are not detectable by conventional genome-wide association analysis.
genome-wide analysis of polymorphisms × soda interaction effect on blood pressures can identify novel genetic loci, which may provide new insights into the pathophysiology of hypertension.
a genetic variant in a gene desert locus can classify persons into subgroups with differential sodium-sensitivity.
